PRO.1.31-33.text: Fools face ruin, but those who listen live safely

PRO.2.18-19.text: The forbidden woman’s house leads to death

PRO.3.15-16.text: Wisdom is worth more than rubies and brings long life

PRO.3.17-18.text: Wisdom’s ways are pleasant and give life

PRO.3.29-30.text: People should not harm or falsely accuse a neighbor

PRO.4.16-17.text: Wicked people live by doing evil and violence

PRO.4.18-19.text: The righteous walk in light, the wicked in darkness

PRO.4.22-23.text: A son must guard his heart, the source of life

PRO.4.24-25.text: A son must speak honestly and look straight ahead

PRO.4.26-27.text: A son must walk a straight path and turn from evil

PRO.5.3-4.text: The forbidden woman’s sweet words end in bitterness

PRO.5.9-10.text: A man could lose his strength and wealth to strangers

PRO.5.11-12.text: A man will groan at the end for hating discipline

PRO.5.13-14.text: A man regrets that he did not listen to his teachers

PRO.5.15-17.text: A husband should stay faithful to his own wife

PRO.5.18-19.text: A husband should rejoice in the wife of his youth

PRO.5.20-21.text: The LORD sees all, so a son should avoid an adulteress

PRO.5.22-23.text: The wicked man is trapped by his own sin and folly

PRO.6.4-5.text: A son must hurry to free himself like a gazelle

PRO.6.14-15.text: A man who plans evil and causes quarrels will suddenly fall

PRO.6.17-19.text: The writer lists seven things the LORD hates

PRO.6.22-23.text: Parents’ teaching guides a son and leads him to life

PRO.6.24-25.text: Teaching keeps a son from the adulteress and her beauty

PRO.6.26-27.text: Adultery costs a man his life, like playing with fire

PRO.6.28-29.text: A man who sleeps with another man’s wife will be punished

PRO.6.30-31.text: A thief must pay back much, even if he stole from hunger

PRO.6.32-33.text: A man who commits adultery destroys himself and is shamed

PRO.6.34-35.text: A jealous husband will show no mercy and accept no payment

PRO.7.4-5.text: A son should love wisdom to be kept from the adulteress

PRO.7.6-7.text: The writer sees a young man without judgment from his window

PRO.7.19-21.text: The woman says her husband is away and lures the young man

PRO.7.22-23.text: The young man follows her like an animal going to a trap

PRO.7.24-25.text: The father urges his sons not to turn to her ways

PRO.7.26-27.text: The adulteress has brought many to death

PRO.8.1-3.text: Wisdom calls out loudly in public places

PRO.8.4-5.text: Wisdom calls all people to learn and gain understanding

PRO.8.6-7.text: Wisdom says her words are noble, true and right

PRO.8.8-9.text: Wisdom says all her words are righteous and plain

PRO.8.10-11.text: Wisdom is worth more than silver, gold and rubies

PRO.8.12-13.text: Wisdom lives with good sense and hates evil and pride

PRO.8.14-16.text: Wisdom gives kings and rulers strength to rule justly

PRO.8.17-18.text: Wisdom loves those who seek her and gives riches and honor

PRO.8.19-21.text: Wisdom’s gifts are better than gold and fill her lovers’ treasuries

PRO.8.22-23.text: Wisdom says the LORD made her first, before the earth

PRO.8.24-25.text: Wisdom says she was born before the seas and mountains

PRO.8.26-27.text: Wisdom was there before God made the earth

PRO.8.28-29.text: Wisdom was there when God set the sea’s limits

PRO.8.30-31.text: Wisdom rejoices beside God and delights in people

PRO.8.32-34.text: Wisdom tells her sons to listen and be wise

PRO.8.35-36.text: Finding Wisdom brings life; hating Wisdom brings death

PRO.9.3-4.text: Wisdom invites people who lack judgment

PRO.9.5-6.text: Wisdom invites the simple to eat, leave folly and live

PRO.9.7-9.text: Wisdom says to correct wise people, not mockers

PRO.9.10-12.text: Fear of the LORD begins wisdom and brings long life

PRO.9.13-15.text: Folly is loud and calls to people passing by

PRO.9.16-18.text: Folly invites the simple, but her guests are dead

PRO.10.4-5.text: Hard work brings wealth; lazy sons bring shame

PRO.10.6-7.text: People remember the righteous, but not the wicked

PRO.10.8-9.text: Wise people accept commands and live with integrity

PRO.10.10-11.text: Foolish lips bring ruin; the righteous speak life

PRO.10.12-13.text: Hatred stirs up conflict, but love forgives wrongs

PRO.10.14-15.text: Wise people store knowledge; fools invite ruin

PRO.10.16-17.text: The righteous find life by accepting correction

PRO.10.18-19.text: Slander is foolish, and holding back words is wise

PRO.10.20-21.text: The righteous speak words that help many people

PRO.10.22-23.text: The LORD’s blessing enriches; fools enjoy shameful acts

PRO.10.24-25.text: The righteous are secure, but the wicked are not

PRO.10.26-27.text: A lazy worker annoys; fearing the LORD gives long life

PRO.10.28-30.text: The righteous have hope and safety; the wicked do not

PRO.10.31-32.text: The righteous speak wisely; the wicked speak wrongly

PRO.11.3-4.text: Integrity guides the upright; riches cannot save

PRO.11.5-6.text: Righteousness saves the upright; the wicked fall

PRO.11.7-8.text: The hope of the wicked dies; the righteous are rescued

PRO.11.9-11.text: A city rejoices when the righteous thrive

PRO.11.15-16.text: Guaranteeing a stranger’s debt brings harm

PRO.11.17-18.text: Kindness helps a person, but cruelty brings trouble

PRO.11.19-20.text: God delights in the blameless, not the perverse

PRO.11.21-22.text: The wicked will be punished; the righteous will escape

PRO.11.23-24.text: Giving freely leads to gain; holding back leads to poverty

PRO.11.25-26.text: The generous prosper, but people curse a grain hoarder

PRO.11.27-28.text: Seeking good brings favor; trusting riches brings a fall

PRO.11.29-29.text: Whoever troubles his family gains nothing

PRO.11.30-31.text: The righteous bear good fruit; sinners are repaid

PRO.12.3-4.text: The righteous stand; a good wife is a crown

PRO.12.5-6.text: The righteous plan justly; wicked words lie in wait

PRO.12.7-8.text: The wicked fall, but the righteous house stands

PRO.12.9-10.text: A humble life with food is better than empty pride

PRO.12.11-12.text: Hard work brings food; chasing fantasies lacks judgment

PRO.12.13-14.text: Evil speech traps people; good speech brings good things

PRO.12.15-16.text: A wise man listens to advice; a fool shows anger at once

PRO.12.17-18.text: Careless words wound, but wise words heal

PRO.12.19-20.text: True words last; lies last only a moment

PRO.12.21-22.text: The LORD hates lying lips and delights in faithful people

PRO.12.23-24.text: Hard workers will rule, but lazy people do forced labor

PRO.12.25-26.text: A good word cheers a heart that worries

PRO.12.27-28.text: Lazy people lose out; righteousness leads to life

PRO.13.1-2.text: A wise son accepts his father’s discipline

PRO.13.3-4.text: Careful speech protects life; the lazy get nothing

PRO.13.5-6.text: The righteous hate lies; the wicked bring shame

PRO.13.7-8.text: Some pretend to be rich, and others pretend to be poor

PRO.13.9-10.text: Pride causes strife, but wise people take advice

PRO.13.11-12.text: Honest work builds wealth; delayed hope hurts the heart

PRO.13.13-14.text: Those who respect instruction are rewarded

PRO.13.15-16.text: Wise people act with knowledge; fools show folly

PRO.13.17-18.text: A faithful envoy heals; ignoring correction brings shame

PRO.13.19-20.text: Walking with the wise makes a person wise

PRO.13.21-22.text: Good people leave an inheritance; sinners face disaster

PRO.13.23-24.text: A loving father disciplines his son

PRO.13.25-25.text: The righteous have enough to eat; the wicked go hungry

PRO.14.17-18.text: A quick temper leads to folly; the prudent gain knowledge

PRO.14.19-20.text: The poor are hated, but many love the rich

PRO.14.21-22.text: Those kind to the poor are blessed; evil planners go astray

PRO.14.23-24.text: Work brings profit, but mere talk brings poverty

PRO.14.26-27.text: Those who fear the LORD find safety and life

PRO.14.28-29.text: A king’s glory is many subjects; the patient understand

PRO.14.32-33.text: The wicked fall by sin; the righteous have refuge in death

PRO.15.19-20.text: The upright path is a highway; a wise son brings joy

PRO.15.29-30.text: The LORD hears the righteous but is far from the wicked

PRO.15.31-32.text: People who accept correction become wise

PRO.15.33-33.text: Fearing the LORD teaches wisdom, and humility brings honor

PRO.16.19-20.text: Humility is better than sharing wealth with the proud

PRO.16.21-22.text: Wise people have understanding and speak pleasantly

PRO.16.23-24.text: A wise heart guides the mouth; pleasant words heal

PRO.16.25-26.text: A way that seems right can end in death

PRO.16.27-28.text: Worthless people spread evil and gossips divide friends

PRO.16.29-30.text: A violent man leads his neighbor to a bad path

PRO.16.31-32.text: Gray hair is honored; patience is better than strength

PRO.16.33-33.text: The LORD decides the result of casting lots

PRO.17.21-22.text: A foolish son brings grief; a joyful heart heals

PRO.17.23-24.text: A wicked man takes bribes; a fool’s eyes wander

PRO.17.25-26.text: Foolish sons grieve fathers; do not punish the innocent

PRO.19.3-4.text: Wealth brings many friends, but the poor are deserted

PRO.19.5-6.text: A false witness will not go unpunished

PRO.19.7-8.text: The poor are avoided by all, but wisdom brings success

PRO.19.9-10.text: A false witness will perish; luxury does not suit a fool

PRO.19.13-14.text: A foolish son and a quarrelsome wife bring trouble

PRO.19.15-16.text: Laziness brings hunger; keeping commands preserves life

PRO.19.17-18.text: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD

PRO.19.26-27.text: A son who mistreats his parents brings shame

PRO.20.23-24.text: The LORD hates dishonest scales and guides people’s steps

PRO.20.27-28.text: The LORD searches people’s hearts; kings need faithfulness

PRO.21.5-6.text: Careful plans bring plenty; wealth from lies is deadly

PRO.21.7-8.text: Violence sweeps away the wicked; the innocent live right

PRO.21.9-10.text: Better to live on a roof than with a quarrelsome wife

PRO.21.11-12.text: Punishing a mocker teaches the simple to be wise

PRO.21.13-14.text: Those who ignore the poor will not be answered

PRO.21.15-16.text: Justice brings joy to the righteous, terror to evildoers

PRO.21.19-20.text: Better to live in the desert than with an angry wife

PRO.21.21-22.text: Pursuing righteousness and love brings life and honor

PRO.21.23-24.text: Guarding the tongue keeps a person safe from distress

PRO.21.25-26.text: Laziness kills, but the righteous give freely

PRO.21.27-28.text: The LORD hates the sacrifice of the wicked

PRO.21.29-29.text: A wicked man is stubborn; an upright man is sure

PRO.22.15-16.text: Discipline drives foolishness out of a child

PRO.22.17-19.text: The teacher urges the reader to hear wise words

PRO.22.20-21.text: The teacher has written thirty sayings of true counsel

PRO.22.24-25.text: Do not make friends with an angry man

PRO.22.26-27.text: Do not promise to pay another man’s debts

PRO.24.19-20.text: Do not envy evildoers, for they have no future

PRO.24.32-34.text: The writer learns that laziness brings poverty

PRO.25.20-20.text: Singing to a sad heart does harm

PRO.25.23-24.text: Gossip causes anger, and a quarrelsome wife brings trouble

PRO.25.25-26.text: Good news refreshes; a righteous man who yields harms

PRO.25.27-28.text: Do not seek too much honey or glory; control anger

PRO.26.1-2.text: Honor does not suit a fool, and a false curse fails

PRO.26.3-4.text: Fools need a rod, and answering them has a risk

PRO.26.5-6.text: Answer a fool, and do not send him with a message

PRO.26.7-8.text: A fool’s proverb and honor for a fool are useless

PRO.26.9-10.text: A fool’s proverb is harmful, and hiring a fool is risky

PRO.26.11-12.text: A fool repeats folly; a proud man has less hope

PRO.26.13-14.text: The lazy man makes excuses and stays in bed

PRO.26.15-16.text: The lazy man is too tired to eat, yet thinks he is wise

PRO.26.17-17.text: Meddling in another’s quarrel is dangerous

PRO.26.18-19.text: A man who deceives a neighbor and says it is a joke

PRO.26.20-21.text: Without gossip a quarrel ends; a quarrelsome man starts strife

PRO.26.22-23.text: Gossip is tempting, and smooth words can hide an evil heart

PRO.26.24-26.text: A hateful man hides his evil, but it will be exposed

PRO.26.27-28.text: Harm to others comes back on the one who does it

PRO.27.1-2.text: Do not boast about tomorrow or praise yourself

PRO.27.3-4.text: A fool’s provoking and jealousy are hard to bear

PRO.27.5-6.text: An honest rebuke from a friend is better than hidden love

PRO.27.7-8.text: Full people refuse honey; wanderers are like lost birds

PRO.27.9-10.text: Stay loyal to friends; a near neighbor is better

PRO.27.11-12.text: A father asks his son to be wise and avoid danger

PRO.27.13-14.text: Debts for strangers are risky; a loud greeting can annoy

PRO.27.15-16.text: A quarreling wife is like endless dripping water

PRO.27.17-18.text: Friends sharpen each other; faithful servants are honored

PRO.27.19-20.text: The heart shows the true person; people are never satisfied

PRO.27.21-22.text: Praise tests a person; a fool does not change

PRO.27.23-25.text: A farmer must care for flocks, because wealth does not last

PRO.27.26-27.text: Flocks give a farmer clothing, money, and food

PRO.28.1-2.text: The righteous are bold; a wise ruler keeps order

PRO.28.3-4.text: Oppressive leaders harm the poor; law keepers resist evil

PRO.28.5-6.text: Those who seek the LORD understand; honesty beats wealth

PRO.28.7-8.text: A wise son keeps the law; wealth from interest is lost

PRO.28.9-10.text: God rejects the prayer of anyone who ignores the law

PRO.28.11-12.text: A poor wise man sees through a proud rich man

PRO.28.13-14.text: God shows mercy to people who confess sin

PRO.28.15-16.text: A wicked ruler is like a lion over helpless people

PRO.28.17-18.text: A murderer runs to ruin; honest people are kept safe

PRO.28.19-20.text: Hard work brings food; hurrying to be rich brings trouble

PRO.28.21-22.text: Showing partiality is wrong; a stingy man will become poor

PRO.28.23-24.text: Honest rebuke is better than flattery; do not rob parents

PRO.28.25-26.text: Those who trust the LORD prosper; self-trust is foolish

PRO.28.27-28.text: Helping the poor is good; people hide when the wicked rule

PRO.29.1-2.text: Stubborn people are broken; wicked rulers make people groan

PRO.29.3-4.text: A wise son brings joy; a just king makes the land stable

PRO.29.5-6.text: Flattery is a net; evil men are trapped by sin

PRO.29.7-8.text: The righteous care for the poor; mockers stir up a city

PRO.29.9-10.text: Arguing with a fool fails; violent men hate the blameless

PRO.29.11-12.text: A fool shows all his anger; a wise man holds it back

PRO.29.13-14.text: A king who judges the poor fairly will last

PRO.29.15-16.text: Correction teaches a child; the wicked will fall

PRO.29.17-18.text: Parents who discipline a son will have rest

PRO.29.19-20.text: A servant ignores words; a hasty speaker has little hope

PRO.29.21-22.text: A spoiled servant brings grief; anger causes fights

PRO.29.23-24.text: Pride brings a man low; humble people receive honor

PRO.29.25-26.text: Trusting the LORD is safer than fearing people

PRO.29.27-27.text: The righteous and the wicked detest each other

PRO.30.1-3.text: Agur says he is weary and lacks wisdom

PRO.30.4-4.text: Agur asks who made the wind, waters and earth

PRO.30.5-6.text: God’s words are flawless, so people must not add to them

PRO.30.7-9.text: Agur asks God for honesty, and neither poverty nor riches

PRO.30.10-10.text: People must not slander a servant to his master

PRO.30.11-12.text: Agur warns of people who curse parents and feel pure

PRO.30.13-14.text: Agur warns of proud people who harm the poor

PRO.30.15-17.text: Agur names things never satisfied; do not mock parents

PRO.30.18-19.text: Agur names four things too wonderful to understand

PRO.30.20-20.text: An adulterous woman says she has done nothing wrong

PRO.30.21-23.text: Agur names four things that make the earth tremble

PRO.30.24-26.text: Small creatures like ants and rock badgers are wise

PRO.30.27-28.text: Agur says locusts and lizards are wise too

PRO.30.29-31.text: Agur names four things that walk with dignity

PRO.30.32-33.text: Agur warns that stirring anger brings strife

PRO.31.1-3.text: Lemuel’s mother warns him about women who ruin kings

PRO.31.4-5.text: Kings must not drink wine, or justice is forgotten

PRO.31.6-7.text: Lemuel’s mother says give wine to those who suffer

PRO.31.8-9.text: Kings must speak for the voiceless and defend the poor

PRO.31.10-12.text: A noble wife is worth more than rubies

PRO.31.13-15.text: The noble wife works hard to feed her household

PRO.31.16-17.text: The noble wife buys a field and works with strength

PRO.31.18-19.text: The noble wife works late spinning thread

PRO.31.20-21.text: The noble wife helps the poor and clothes her household

PRO.31.22-23.text: The noble wife dresses well; her husband is respected

PRO.31.24-25.text: The noble wife sells linen and has strength and honor

PRO.31.26-27.text: The noble wife speaks wisely and manages her home

PRO.31.28-29.text: The noble wife’s children and husband praise her

PRO.31.30-31.text: A woman who fears the LORD should be praised
